editorial:
Imagine a world where you can just pay someone to make your crush fall in love with you. That is exactly what happens here. You meet a clever magician who makes a living selling fake love spells to desperate people. He is great at playing people for fools until he meets a beautiful woman who is about to get married. Instead of just taking her money, he decides he wants her for himself. The vibe is a mix of old-school mystery and creepy magic, making you wonder if the spells are actually fake or if there is something real and dangerous going on behind the scenes.

What really works is how the tension builds as the magician gets more obsessed. The acting is solid, and the twists keep you guessing about who is actually in control. While some parts move a bit slow, the payoff is totally worth it. If you love weird vintage horror, you should definitely track this down. It looks amazing if you can find the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection, but renting it on Apple TV is also a great way to experience it. It is a wild ride that feels like a dark fairy tale.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a big twist where the magician's greed and lust backfire on him. After trying to steal the bride using his dark arts, he finds out that he is not the only one who knows how to use magic. The bride and her partner outsmart him, turning his own spells against him. He ends up losing everything and meeting a grim fate, proving that playing with people's hearts and dark magic always ends badly.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage Asian horror and stories about magic gone wrong.
